rule.title: Rules check
rule.official: The Controller of Budget found that counties together spent {wages} of total revenue on wages, above the {limit} limit, and that some counties did not pay their full wage bill, which makes their ratios look lower. Below is our own check for this county, using the same method.
rule.development.q: Did the budget set aside enough for development?
rule.development.line: Share of the {fy} budget for development in {name}. The minimum is {limit}.
rule.development.law: The law: "over the medium term a minimum of thirty percent of the county government's budget shall be allocated to the development expenditure". This shows one year, and the rule looks across several, so one year alone does not settle it.
rule.wages.q: How much of its revenue went on wages?
rule.wages.line: Wages and benefits as a share of total revenue in {name}, {fy}. The limit is {limit}.
rule.wages.law: The law: the limit "shall not exceed thirty five (35) percent of the county government's total revenue", leaving out revenue from extractive natural resources such as oil and coal. Revenue here is what the county reported, including money carried forward, as in the Controller of Budget's own ratios.
depth.osrQ: How much did the county collect itself?
depth.grantsQ: How much came in additional allocations?
depth.grantsLine: {pct} of the {target} budgeted in {fy}, from the national government and development partners.
depth.billsQ: What did the county owe suppliers at the end of the year?
depth.billsLine: Trade payables at 30 June 2026, the county executive and assembly together. That equals {pct} of the {fy} budget.
depth.billsNoneWhy: The Controller of Budget says {name} did not report any for 30 June 2026. That is not the same as owing nothing.
question.bills: {name} owed suppliers {amount} at 30 June 2026. What is the payment plan, and which bills are oldest?
question.osr: {name} collected {pct} of its own-revenue target in {fy}. Which sources fell short, and what will change this year?
